{{Short description|Georgian astrophysicist}}
[[File:Jumber Lominadze 1986.jpg|thumb|Jumber Lominadze in 1986]]
'''Jumber Lominadze''' ({{lang-ka|ჯუმბერ ლომინაძე}} {{Audio|En-us-Dzhumber Lominadze from Georgia pronunciation (Voice of America).ogg|[dʒumbɛr lɔminɑdzɛ]}}; 20 September 1930 – 20 January 2014) was a [[Georgia (country)|Georgian]] astrophysicist associated with the [[Georgian Academy of Sciences]].

==Biography==
Born in [[Tbilisi]], [[Georgian SSR]], Lominadze was trained as a physicist at the [[Tbilisi State University]] (1949–1951) and [[Moscow State University]] (1951–1955). After working for the Russian center nuclear program at [[Snezhinsk|Chelyabinsk-70]] from 1956 to 1958, he returned to Tbilisi where he worked for the Georgian Academy of Sciences for decades. He obtained a doctorate in physics and mathematics in 1974 and became a professor in 1982. He was elected as a Corresponding Member of the Georgian Academy of Sciences in 1979 and Academician in 1988. Lominadze directed the [[Georgian National Astrophysical Observatory|Abastumani Astrophysical Observatory]] from 1992 to 2000 and then the Plasma Astrophysics Center thereof from 2000 to 2006. He chaired the Georgian Space Agency from 2003 to 2006 and headed the Center for Space Studies at the Georgian Institute of Geophysics from 2006 until his death in 2014. Lominadze authored about 250 scholarly works, including his principal monograph ''Cyclotron Waves in Plasma'', which appeared in Russian in 1975 and in English in 1981.<ref name="gnas">{{cite web|title=Jumber Lominadze. Curriculum Vitae |url=http://www.science.org.ge/academic-cons.html |publisher=Georgian National Academy of Sciences |accessdate=20 January 2014 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201162817/http://www.science.org.ge/academic-cons.html |archivedate= 1 February 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Avrorin|first=É.N.|author2=Balebanov, V. M. |author3=Boyarchuk, A. A. |title=Jumber Lominadze (In Honor of His 70th Birthday)|journal=[[Plasma Physics Reports]]|date=February 2001|volume=27|issue=2|pages=178–179|doi=10.1134/1.1348497|bibcode=2001PlPhR..27..178A |s2cid=123560144|issn=1562-6938|display-authors=etal}}</ref>

Beyond his academic activities, Lominadze was involved in the public life of Georgia during the presidency of [[Eduard Shevardnadze]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Kelly|first=Tom|title=Cabinet Purge Adds New Urgency To Georgians' Crash Course In Democracy|url=http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/1998-07-31/news/9807300303_1_georgia-academy-election-officials-president-eduard-shevardnadze|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202092936/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/1998-07-31/news/9807300303_1_georgia-academy-election-officials-president-eduard-shevardnadze|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 2, 2014|accessdate=20 January 2014|newspaper=Sun-Sentinel|date=July 31, 1998}}</ref> He chaired the [[Election Administration of Georgia|Georgian Central Election Commission]] from 1997 to 2003 and oversaw four elections, those for local self-government in 1998 and 2002, [[Georgian parliamentary election, 1999|parliamentary]] in 1999, and [[Georgian presidential election, 2000|presidential]] in 2000.<ref name="gnas"/><ref>{{cite web|title=Georgia — History of Elections 1990–2010|url=http://cesko.ge/files/TEA/archevnebisistoria/enghistory.pdf|publisher=Central Election Commission|accessdate=20 January 2014|pages=5, 11, 12, 13|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304000519/http://www.cesko.ge/files/TEA/archevnebisistoria/enghistory.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He died on 20 January 2014, aged 83.<ref>{{cite news|title=გარდაიცვალა აკადემიკოსი ჯუმბერ ლომინაძე|trans-title=Academician Jumber Lominadze dies|url=http://www.radiotavisupleba.ge/archive/geo-news/20140120/1001/1001.html?id=25235819|accessdate=20 January 2014|date=20 January 2014|agency=Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty|language=Georgian}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Lominadze was awarded the [[Orders, decorations, and medals of Georgia|Order of Vakhtang Gorgasali, 3rd Rank]] in 2000 and the State Prize in 2002.<ref name="gnas"/>
